sections.content: How many people are "police community support officers"?

10,775 people

were counted on the census as "police community support officers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Police Community Support Officers (PCSOs) support the local police force by patrolling the streets to provide a visible and reassuring presence and to tackle a range of crime and disorder problems.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "police community support officers" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 35 to 39 years. Of the whole working population 11.5% were aged 35 to 39 years. For people working as "police community support officers", 13.3% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "police community support officers" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "police community support officers" included:

  • transport and distribution clerks and assistants
  • food, drink and tobacco process operatives
  • stock control clerks and assistants

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

A similar number of men and women had this job

Among people working as "police community support officers" there were a similar number of men and women (50.5% compared with 49.5%).

This means "police community support officers" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "community and civil enforcement occupations".

Men made up 50.5% and women made up 49.5% of "police community support officers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "police community support officers" included:

  • advertising accounts managers and creative directors
  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "police community support officers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "police community support officers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "police community support officers", 9.7% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (89.2% compared with 10.8%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (99.5%) than self-employed (0.5%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
